title: Crosslink: Ops + SLOs 30/60/90 collaboration playbook
content:
Purpose: quick-working playbook to align product, platform, SRE, and infra on SLO targets, error-budget ops and a 30/60/90 collaborative runway for the next model-serving rollout. This is intentionally pragmatic — mix of action items, meeting cadence, and templates we can copy into feature-team onboarding.

What this doc is NOT: final governance doc. It’s a field playbook to run coordinated experiments and get everyone to the same incident/rollback decisions quickly.

Top-level goals
- Establish a single source of truth for SLOs and signal ownership for model-serving endpoints.
- Define error-budget consumption thresholds and automated/ manual escalation triggers.
- Run a 30/60/90 sequence of cross-team checkpoints to validate telemetry, capacity, and fallback behavior before GA.
- Reduce blast radius with fast rollback paths and routing fallback to lightweight model variants.

Stakeholders (who to ping)
- SRE lead: Aisha Khan — overall oncall/runbook steward
- Platform eng: Miguel Ramirez — autoscaling and capacity testing
- Product & Hosting: Claire O'Neill — customer-impact assessment and launch gating
- Model serving runtime: Samir Gupta — KV cache and batching behavior
- Solutions Eng / CS: TBD per-customer for bespoke SLAs

Roles & responsibilities (working draft)
- SRE: define SLI computations, own alerts, runbook lifecycle, post-incident notes.
- Platform: run capacity sims, maintain canary clusters, own deployment automation.
- Product: approve SLO targets and determine acceptable user-facing degradation bands.
- Runtime: provide low-latency fallback artifacts and quantized model variants.
- CS/SE: runway validation with top customers, acceptability sign-off for GA.

30/60/90 plan (high level)
- Day 0–30 (Discovery + quick wins):
  - Inventory current endpoints & owners (owner list in Jira SRE-482).
  - Agree on 3 canonical SLIs (p99 latency, token success rate, model-responsiveness error-rate).
  - Lightweight instrumentation sweep: confirm traces, request IDs and KV cache metrics are emitted.
  - Run smoke canary for one non-critical model to validate metrics pipeline.
  - Deliverable: SLI definitions + baseline dashboard (Grafana link in Confluence).
- Day 31–60 (Stabilize + policy):
  - Run capacity simulations at 2x, 5x expected QPS for the critical endpoint group.
  - Build automated gating: if p99 > threshold OR error-rate uses > 20% of EB in 1h -> trigger circuit-breaker.
  - Create runbook templates for three ticket tiers: P0 (service down), P1 (degraded latency), P2 (minor regression).
  - Deliverable: Canary gating rules, runbook v0.1, automated rollback playbook.
- Day 61–90 (Hardening + rollout):
  - Run cross-team tabletop (SRE, platform, runtime, product) using real incident scenarios.
  - Start phased rollout to majority traffic with automatic fallback to smaller model variant under heavy error-budget consumption.
  - Formalize SLA/commitment language for Dedicated customers; produce handoff doc for Private deploys.
  - Deliverable: Launch checklist, final runbooks, stakeholder signoffs.

Error budget policy (example)
- SLO: p95 latency < 1200ms, availability 99.5% over 30d window (example only).
- Error budget = 1 - availability target.
- Consumption bands:
  - Green: < 25% EB used in 7d -> normal ops.
  - Yellow: 25–50% EB used in 7d -> alert on Slack #sre-ops, add extra sampling for traces, escalate to platform.
  - Orange: 50–80% EB -> mandatory triage meeting within 2h, reduce non-critical workloads, enable burst protection.
  - Red: > 80% EB -> automatic routing to fallback model, partial traffic freeze, exec notification and customer comms draft.

Canary & rollback template (notes)
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h if no gates tripped.
- Metrics to watch during canary: p50/p95/p99, token error rate, memory pressure, KV cache hit ratio, tail-latency CPU/GPU stall metrics.
- Quick rollback steps (ops): 1) Pause rollout via deployment UI (link), 2) Switch route to previous variant, 3) Expand circuit-breaker to reject suspect input patterns, 4) Engage oncall.

Telemetry checklist (must-have instrumentation)
- Request-id propagated end-to-end.
- Token-level generation errors surfaced as structured metrics.
- KV cache hit/miss per request and cumulative miss-rate.
- Batching/packing metrics (batch size distribution).
- Autoscaler decisions & queue lengths exported as metrics.

Communication plan
- Alerts: send to #sre-prod (critical) and #sre-watch (info), use PagerDuty for P0/P1.
- Daily sync (first 30 days): 15min standup at 10:00 PST to track canary health (rotate note-taker).
- Weekly review (30/60/90): 60min cross-functional review on Fridays; capture decisions in Confluence and link to JIRA epic.
- Exec pulse: 2x week summary during active rollouts when EB > 50%.

Runbook templates (skeleton)
- Triage notes: initial hypothesis, evidence (links to traces), immediate mitigations, rollback actions, communication.
- Post-incident: action items, owner, ETA, risk rating.
- Lessons learned: telemetry gaps, test-case gaps, config knobs to adjust.

Staffing & rotations (practical)
- Oncall: SRE owns primary pager for model-serving endpoints; platform provides secondary rotation for scaling incidents.
- War-room roster for rollouts: 2 SREs, 1 Platform engineer, 1 Runtime engineer, 1 Product PM, 1 Solutions/CS rep.
- Escalation ladder: SRE -> Head SRE (Aisha) -> Head Platform (Miguel) -> CTO (if P0).

Failure modes we care about (initial list)
- Long-tail latencies from batching packing mismatch.
- KV cache corruption or eviction storms causing token regen cascades.
- Autoscaler misconfiguration leading to cold-start queues.
- Model quantization regressions causing increased token-level errors.

Testing & validation playbook
- Chaos test harness for cache eviction (small-scale, non-prod).
- Load-test jobs that exercise both steady-state and spike traffic patterns; tie to CI so runs can be triggered by infra changes.
- Regression evaluation: test promptsets and automated eval pipeline to detect quality regressions tied to SLOs.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Which SLO window do we standardize on across hosted vs dedicated? (30d vs 7d vs 14d) -- need product input.
- Do we allow feature teams to adopt stricter SLAs than platform default? (yes, but how to bill/reserve)
- Thresholds for automatic fallback are heuristic — propose starting with 20% EB in 1h for orange. Opinions?

Immediate next actions (owner tags)
- Jordan: finalize SLI definitions and commit to dashboard by 2026-02-17. (JIRA-SRE-482)
- Miguel: schedule capacity sim runs and provide baseline by 2026-02-24.
- Aisha: draft runbook template and run tabletop on 2026-03-04.
- Claire: compile customer-impact matrix for Dedicated customers by 2026-02-20.

Quick notes to self (informal)
- Keep playbook lightweight. Avoid 40-page policy that no one reads.
- Reuse existing runbook fragments from infra repo PR-912.
- We should capture sample customer comms for EB-red scenarios (email + status page templates).

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Crosslink+Ops+SLO+Playbook
- Jira epic: JIRA-SRE-482
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912
- Dashboard (placeholder): grafana://model-serving-slo-overview

Status log (mini)
- 2026-02-10: doc created (Jordan)
- 2026-02-12: initial stakeholder sync; agreed on p99/p95/p50 set up
- 2026-02-16: alerted to missing batch-size metric in runtime — flagged to Samir

End of working draft.

Unresolved: need product agreement on windows and whether to enable automatic fallback by default for hosted customers.
